verdict.line: You lose if you let mini Gnar eat free Parrrley pokes before level 6; you win the 53% head-to-head once Mega Gnar and Trinity Force come online.

brief.thesis: Gnar's Q (Boomerang Throw, 1100 range) outranges Gangplank's Q (Parrrley, 625 range) all game, but Parrrley's 5-second cooldown lets Gangplank poke far more often than Gnar can answer before level 6 — that's why OP.GG tags him for lane advantage even though Gnar wins the head-to-head 53% of the time over 202 games. The lane is a rage-bar race: mini Gnar loses the poke exchange early, Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) stun and E (Crunch) AoE burst win it once he's reliably transforming.

theirWindow.when: Parrrley off cooldown and you're inside 625
theirWindow.what: Step back outside 625 range or break line of sight in brush — Parrrley needs a visible target, and at levels 1-2 before your E (Hop) is online this is the only way to deny it for free.

yourWindow.when: right after he lands a Parrrley
yourWindow.what: Close immediately and throw Q (Boomerang Throw) or trade autos — his poke tool is down for a full 5 seconds, longer than your W (Hyper) cooldown of 7s, so you out-trade him in that window every time.

start.why: Doran's Blade runs 55.6% over 108 games versus Doran's Shield's 47.5% here — the sustained damage matters more than the shield's regen since you want to win trades outright, not just survive his poison passive.

boots.why: 89.2% pick rate at 52.4% win rate; Gangplank's harass is mostly basic attacks plus his Grog-Soaked Blade poison on-hit, and Steelcaps' flat AA reduction blunts that far better than Mercury's Treads' tenacity, which he doesn't apply much CC to use.

core.why: The highest-win-rate path (66.7% over 30 games) starts here — the MS, damage, and proc give mini Gnar the stats to actually close the range gap instead of just poking at it.
Stacks armor shred on your Q and auto trades, which matters since Gangplank has no armor-shred answer and your window to punish is every short trade, not one long fight.

Completes the top win-rate build (66.7%) — the active slow and tankiness let Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) and W (Wallop) all-in window actually stick instead of letting him kite out with Raise Morale's MS buff.

situational.when: you're falling behind and need the shield to survive his all-ins rather than Randuin's active slow
his Grog-Soaked Blade poison stacks are chunking your sustain faster than you can trade back
he's ahead and out-trading you on autos, since the grievous wounds shuts down any healing he picks up

runes.keystoneWhy: Fleet Footwork is the higher-sample, higher-pick keystone here (57.5% WR, 30.8% pick) — the heal-on-hit and burst MS let you both sustain through Parrrley poke and close distance to punish it. Master-tier players instead run Lethal Tempo (53.2% WR across 1,842 games) if you want to lean into longer attack-speed-scaling trades rather than disengage-and-reset.

summoners.why: Flash + Teleport is the default (62% pick, 49% WR) since this lane is a slow rage-bar grind and Teleport lets you reset waves and join sidelane fights. Flash + Ignite (56.1% WR) adds kill pressure during the level 2-5 trading window where Parrrley exchanges are already close. Exhaust + Flash (65.2% WR, smaller sample) is the pick if you expect him to all-in off Raise Morale's AD/MS buff and want to shut that down directly.

playing.title: Break his Parrrley sightline
playing.detail: Parrrley needs a visible enemy unit to fire at; use brush or minion cover to deny it for free, especially at levels 1-2 before your E (Hop) gives you an escape.

playing.title: Poke at 1100, not 625
playing.detail: Throw Q (Boomerang Throw) at max range and walk forward to catch the return — catching it cuts its cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s base) and stacks Rage without ever entering his 625-range poke zone.

playing.title: Weave Hyper into every trade
playing.detail: Mini Gnar's W triggers off both attacks and spells for bonus damage and Move Speed on a 7s cooldown — use it every time you commit to a Q or auto trade to win the MS race in and out.

playing.title: Bait Remove Scurvy before you all-in
playing.detail: His W (Remove Scurvy, cd 22-18s) clears CC and heals him; don't dump your E (Hop) or R (GNAR!) into a half-committed trade just to get cleansed — force him to use it on a weak engage first, then all-in once it's down.

playing.title: All-in the instant you transform
playing.detail: Mega Gnar's W (Wallop) stuns an area in front of him and E (Crunch) damages everything around him on landing — pop Rage into Mega form right as he commits to a trade so the stun locks him into the burst.

playing.title: Don't overreact to Cannon Barrage
playing.detail: His R (Cannon Barrage, cd 120/115/110/120/120s) has global range and slows plus damages an area over time, but it telegraphs before it lands — it's a zoning and split-push tool, not a lane all-in threat, so don't play scared of it mid-trade.

brief.patchCaveat: Build order, rune pages, boots, summoners, and every win rate above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning for why the poke race and Mega Gnar timing swing this lane is my own read, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Try to gain control over Powder Keg(E). Hide in brushes while kiting to avoid being hit with his (Q).
